subject: Administrative Leave of Veterans Services Director
overview: The City Council addressed several business permit requests and municipal zoning reports while residents and veterans protested the administrative leave of the Veterans Services Director. The body also approved various traffic safety improvements and resolutions regarding public transit and affordable housing.

items.title: Public Hearing on Dunkin' Donuts Extended Hours
items.summary: The council approved a special permit for the Dunkin' Donuts at 283 Middlesex Avenue to operate from 4:00 am to 7:00 am daily.

items.title: Public Hearing on Superior Auto Body Class 4 License
items.summary: The council approved a Class 4 license for an automotive repair and auto body shop at 435 Riverside Avenue.

items.title: Clear Channel Digital Billboard Replacement
items.summary: Approved a petition to replace digital billboard faces at 162 Mystic Avenue with more efficient hardware.

items.title: Brooks Elementary Fall Festival Food Truck Permit
items.summary: Approved a food truck permit for a fundraising event at Brooks Elementary School.

items.title: Legal Services Budget Amendment
items.summary: Referred a request to increase the fiscal year 2022 legal services budget from $26,600 to $81,600 to the Committee of the Whole.

items.title: Non-Union Compensation Plan Amendments
items.summary: The council approved the first reading of an ordinance amendment adding four positions to the city compensation plan after reviewing salary ranges.

items.title: Affordable Housing Appropriation on Fellsway West
items.summary: Approved the appropriation of $355,000 from the housing reserve to create three affordable units on Fellsway West.

items.title: Polystyrene Ban Advancement
items.summary: Referred a proposed ban on polystyrene packaging to the Committee of the Whole for further discussion.

items.title: Administrative Leave of Michael Durham
items.summary: The council heard extensive public testimony regarding the placement of Veterans Services Director Michael Durham on administrative leave and passed a motion requesting his immediate reinstatement and an emergency meeting to discuss the operation of his office.

items.title: Carding, West, and North Street Safety Improvements
items.summary: Referred a request for traffic calming measures and crosswalks at the intersection to an on-site Committee of the Whole meeting.

items.title: Ceremonial Recognitions and Condolences
items.summary: The council approved resolutions celebrating the 50th wedding anniversaries of the Gliona and Pittorino families, the 85th birthday of Jack McDevitt, and several expressions of condolence.

items.title: Central Avenue and Otis Street Safety Measures
items.summary: Approved the installation of a blinking stoplight at Central Avenue and Park Street and a speed bump on Otis Street.

items.title: Amici’s Pizza 30th Anniversary Recognition
items.summary: The council commended Amici's Pizza for 30 years of business in West Medford.

items.title: Police Department Retirements
items.summary: Recognized Captain John Conway and Lieutenant Mark Rudolph for their retirement following decades of service.

items.title: Riverside Avenue Bocce Court Repairs
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting that the Parks Department replace sand with proper stone dust at the municipal bocce courts.

items.title: West Medford Commuter Rail Accessibility Funding
items.summary: Approved a letter of support for state funding to upgrade the West Medford station to meet ADA accessibility standards.

items.title: Mystic Valley Parkway and High Street Safety Improvements
items.summary: Requested that the DCR implement urgent safety improvements at the mixer lane and address hazards near the Craddock Bridge.

items.title: Winthrop Street Pedestrian Safety Beacons
items.summary: Approved a request for rapid flashing beacons at the Winthrop Street intersections with West and Summer Streets.

items.title: Highland Avenue Speeding Mitigation
items.summary: Approved a request for the Transportation Director to coordinate with MassDOT regarding speeding and crosswalk painting on Highland Avenue.

items.title: Silver Line Extension Advocacy
items.summary: Requested a report on city efforts to ensure the proposed Silver Line extension includes stops at Wellington Station and Route 16.

items.title: Comprehensive Plan Resident Outreach
items.summary: Approved a resolution to include comprehensive plan informational materials in city tax and utility mailings.

items.title: Report on Legal and Administrative Claims
items.summary: Requested a report from the City Solicitor on the number and status of non-personnel legal claims filed against the city since the start of the year.

items.title: Suspended Bus Routes and MBTA Assessments
items.summary: Referred a request for a meeting with state officials and the MBTA regarding suspended bus routes and the legality of withholding city assessments to the Committee of the Whole.

items.title: Riverside Plaza and Sloan Square Safety
items.summary: Referred a request for increased patrols and social service outreach in Medford Square to the Public Safety Subcommittee.

items.title: Parking Revenue Metrics Request
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting year-to-date parking revenue data from Republic Parking ahead of the program's transition in-house.

items.title: Usher Road and Cedar Road Flooding Investigations
items.summary: Referred several reports of severe residential flooding to a Committee of the Whole meeting with the city engineer and DPW.

items.title: Police Retirement Recognitions
items.summary: Commended Officer Guy Leone and Sergeant David Bono for 36 years of service upon their retirement.

items.title: Committee Report and Records
items.summary: The council accepted a zoning committee report and approved several sets of meeting records while tabling others.
